notes: HE2 tooling seed inventory. It demonstrates every governed status class against the J1/H2 incidents and the seven required cross-cutting interactions. It deliberately does NOT claim coverage: no node carries evidence, PASS is absent, and all uncovered work is registered in coverage-debt.json. Full risk-first business backfill is authorized separately under HE3.

nodes.entry: direct route: public reset endpoint reached while global interceptor is active
nodes.action: submit reset completion to public endpoint expecting a neutral 4xx
nodes.ui_oracle: neutral error copy is rendered; no account-existence signal; no session chrome appears
nodes.navigation_oracle: route stays on the public reset route; no redirect to /login or /retail/login
nodes.network_oracle: reset request returns 4xx exactly once; no token-refresh request is issued
nodes.session_oracle: auth store remains anonymous; no access or refresh token is written
nodes.persistence_security_oracle: password unchanged; reset token not consumed; no secret in response body
nodes.notes: J1/H2-B incident: public reset 401 was redirected by the global session interceptor before the page could render its neutral error.

nodes.entry: direct route: public endpoint invoked with skipAuthInterceptors while a stale contextual session exists
nodes.action: call public credential endpoint with explicit no-auth request semantics
nodes.ui_oracle: workflow completes; stale-session banner does not appear; no forced re-login
nodes.navigation_oracle: final route is the workflow's own success route; history has no /login entry
nodes.network_oracle: public request carries no Authorization header; no refresh request is triggered by this call
nodes.session_oracle: pre-existing (stale) tokens are not silently refreshed or cleared by the public call
nodes.persistence_security_oracle: no credential rotation side effect; response contains no token material

nodes.entry: api endpoint: tenant-scoped read of a resource owned by workspace B
nodes.action: request another tenant's resource through the tenant search path
nodes.network_oracle: request returns 403/404; response body contains no cross-tenant identifiers
nodes.session_oracle: session unchanged; workspace context cannot be switched by payload tampering
nodes.persistence_security_oracle: no row from another schema is readable or writable; search_path stays pinned to caller schema

nodes.entry: api endpoint: rate-limited route under burst
nodes.action: exceed the anonymous rate limit on a rate-limited route
nodes.ui_oracle: user-visible rate-limit message; next supported action (retry after window) is available
nodes.navigation_oracle: route is stable; no redirect or history mutation on 429
nodes.network_oracle: 429 response carries rate-limit headers; no further upstream requests after rejection
nodes.session_oracle: no session is created by rejected requests
nodes.persistence_security_oracle: rejected requests produce no tenant data writes; no credential material in 429 body

nodes.action: replay the same payment declaration confirm (duplicate click and replayed request)
nodes.ui_oracle: no duplicate confirmation UI state; single declaration shown after refresh
nodes.network_oracle: replayed confirm returns the original result (same record id); no second mutation request is processed
nodes.persistence_security_oracle: exactly one declaration row and one ledger effect; same key with different payload is rejected

nodes.action: retry a mutation with the same idempotency key, then with the same key but different payload
nodes.network_oracle: same-key same-payload returns cached result; same-key different-payload returns 409-class rejection
nodes.persistence_security_oracle: replay cache entry is scoped to tenant and endpoint; no cross-tenant cache leak

nodes.action: consume a used reset token, then exercise expired, revoked, and forged variants
nodes.ui_oracle: neutral invalid-token copy for every invalid variant; identical copy across variants
nodes.navigation_oracle: invalid tokens land on the neutral error state, not /login; valid token lands on the reset form
nodes.network_oracle: each invalid variant is a single 4xx; no retry storm; no refresh call
nodes.session_oracle: no session is created by any invalid token variant
nodes.persistence_security_oracle: used token stays consumed (single-use holds under replay); password unchanged; token hash never returned

nodes.action: accept an expired invitation, then a revoked and an already-accepted one
nodes.ui_oracle: neutral expired/invalid invitation copy; supported recovery action offered where applicable
nodes.navigation_oracle: expired invitation does not create history entries into authenticated areas
nodes.network_oracle: single 4xx per invalid invitation; no acceptance mutation request is sent
nodes.session_oracle: no session issued for invalid invitations
nodes.persistence_security_oracle: membership unchanged; invitation state machine not advanced by invalid attempts

nodes.entry: api endpoint: payment confirm with induced mid-transaction failure
nodes.action: force a failure after partial writes inside the tenant transaction
nodes.network_oracle: failure response is a structured 5xx; no partial-success 2xx
nodes.persistence_security_oracle: all writes inside the boundary are rolled back; no orphan ledger entry or declaration state survives

nodes.ui_oracle: drawer opens/closes cleanly; long content scrolls; form submission feedback visible without layout overflow
nodes.navigation_oracle: drawer closes on route change and Escape; back/forward restores correct route without stuck backdrop

nodes.session_oracle: session and workspace survive navigation and back/forward
nodes.persistence_security_oracle: form submission produces exactly one record across drawer open/close cycles

nodes.action: discover, enter, complete, and leave the forgot-password journey through supported UI only
nodes.ui_oracle: entry link visible on login; neutral confirmation copy; reset form reachable from delivered token
nodes.navigation_oracle: full route chain login -> forgot -> email -> reset -> login is traversable without manual URL entry
nodes.network_oracle: each step hits its expected endpoint; no protected call before authentication
nodes.session_oracle: anonymous throughout until password reset completes; then standard login applies
nodes.persistence_security_oracle: reset email delivered exactly once; token single-use enforced; no enumeration signal at any step
nodes.notes: J1/H2 incident: the capability existed below the UI before it was navigable.

nodes.entry: api endpoint: neutral public workflow compared across two accounts
nodes.action: compare neutral responses for existing and non-existing accounts
nodes.ui_oracle: visible copy identical for both accounts
nodes.network_oracle: same status class and semantic key set; volatile metadata (timestamp/request id) validated for presence and format only, via a named allowlist
nodes.session_oracle: no client-state difference between the two accounts
nodes.persistence_security_oracle: no account-existence side channel; unknown fields fail closed
nodes.notes: J1/H2 incident: raw-byte equality treated a legitimate per-request timestamp as semantic drift.

nodes.capability: tenant-local catalog product and stable sellable-unit identity
nodes.entry: full stack: create one product with multiple packaging units and place an order
nodes.action: create packaging variants, stock them independently, and create an order using the selected stable UUID
nodes.ui_oracle: each packaging option is independently selectable and unavailable products are hidden from the retailer
nodes.navigation_oracle: desktop and 390px catalog journeys complete through supported routes without manual URL entry
nodes.network_oracle: order request carries sellable_unit_id; a mismatched ID and SKU code or a cross-tenant ID is rejected
nodes.session_oracle: tenant and actor context remain unchanged throughout product and order mutations
nodes.persistence_security_oracle: CatalogProduct owns shared presentation; each SKU UUID owns inventory; reservation and movement rows retain that UUID without code lookup
nodes.notes: SKU-M1 inventory addition. No protocol delta is applicable because no existing inventory node is removed, renamed, reordered, or reclassified.

nodes.capability: immutable order snapshots across catalog rename and deactivation
nodes.entry: full stack: existing stable order followed by catalog mutation
nodes.action: rename and deactivate the source product after order creation, then read and print the historical order
nodes.ui_oracle: historical name, SKU code, unit, quantity, price, and amount remain the captured transaction values
nodes.navigation_oracle: historical order remains reachable after the source sellable unit is unavailable
nodes.network_oracle: order response returns snapshots and stable source ID without replacing snapshots through a live catalog join
nodes.persistence_security_oracle: catalog writes do not update order_items snapshots; legacy null identities remain null unless unique reservation evidence exists
nodes.notes: Migration counterexamples include no reservation, exactly one reservation identity, and conflicting reservation identities; code and name inference are forbidden.

nodes.capability: order state authority: single locked-fresh command writer, explicit dispatch, pre-lock inventory discipline, post-commit notifications, fail-closed paid cancellation; R2 adds per-order credit holds — confirm opens a hold (binding cache += total), cancel settles and releases it, a credit payment converts it into exposure counted exactly once, full cash/transfer settles it to zero, and the 039 migration preflight proves the binding-cache identity
nodes.entry: direct routes: POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/confirm|cancel|fulfill|return, POST /api/v1/client/orders/{id}/cancel, pay via CanonicalPaymentService
nodes.resource_state: orders across DRAFT..RETURNED with reservations, stock, bindings credit aggregate
nodes.input_state: valid lifecycle requests, concurrent same-order pairs, cross-order same-key payment replays, stale identity-map and swapped-pointer declarations, permission-less and cross-tenant tokens, injected non-domain faults, SQL-corrupted over-collected payment history
nodes.action: drive the full lifecycle, race confirm/cancel/pay and fulfill/return on two orders x two SKUs with reverse item order, pay confirmed orders by credit (hold conversion) and cash/transfer (hold settlement), cancel confirmed orders (hold settle/release), inject faults after the state write and during the second per-item inventory write, attempt generic-transition bypasses and no-actor confirms
nodes.network_oracle: exactly one writer endpoint per state change; generic transition refuses command-owned targets; paid/partially_paid cancel returns 409 REFUND_WORKFLOW_NOT_IMPLEMENTED; client repeated/paid cancel returns stable 409 CANCEL_NOT_ALLOWED; credit-hold contract violations (missing converted hold, remaining mismatch, over-collected or corrupt history) return 409 CREDIT_HOLD_MISMATCH / PAYMENT_HISTORY_INTEGRITY
nodes.session_oracle: permission-less JWT denied before writes; cross-tenant request is a neutral 404
nodes.persistence_security_oracle: confirm opens a per-order credit hold (binding cache += total) and posts zero receivable/revenue/payment ledger entries; cancel releases owned reservations with aggregate updates and settles/releases the hold exactly once; a credit payment converts the hold into actual credit exposure (one total of binding movement, never double-counted in the receivables summary); full cash/transfer settlement reduces the hold to zero; the 039 backfill follows the C3 state matrix and its preflight proves the binding cache equals the exposure-only formula; over-collected or invalid payment history is a named refusal on the write path and both receivables reads; whole-request rollback restores the exact before-vector on injected faults; notification intents dispatch only post-commit to real retailer contacts; snapshots and identity_status never rewritten
nodes.notes: Author-executed (ZCode under Codex-L supervision) on task PG16; independent rerun pending (KILO_OR_OPENCODE2 gate). F3: legacy-face extension — legacy DRAFT cancel is a pure status transition, legacy-with-reservations cancel derives its stock set from ACTIVE reservations (reservation.sku_id), fulfill/return reject NULL sellable identity with a controlled 409 before inventory or return-ledger effects; mutation classifier voids ANY collection/setup/teardown ERROR. R2 closes the R1 credit-hold gap: per-order holds (order_credit_holds) give cancel exactly what to settle/release, credit payment converts the same hold (exposure counted exactly once), and the 039 preflight proves the binding cache identity — the three former F1 KNOWN-RED faces are GREEN regression oracles (CREDIT_HOLD_PERSISTENCE_DECISION_REQUIRED is resolved and removed). R1 mutation runner executes strictly inside a disposable detached worktree (authoritative tree never a write target, in-memory byte+mode restore, no git-restore path). E1 source revision (11ecbe85): bootstrap reconcile validates per-order effective-history legality and the per-order hold lifecycle contract before any aggregate (read-only, fail-closed, no lifecycle rewrites; empty new-tenant history stays the legal positive control; the bootstrap touch surface is four read-only validation queries in _reconcile_credit_holds, registered in the commit message); canonical credit-sale collection requires exactly one effective credit on the seam shared by direct pay and declaration confirmation; the cash/transfer settlement writes the binding cache last (hold -> payment/receipt/ledger -> binding) in one transaction.
